 Outlook Seth McGowan 
 Seth McGowan at Houston — Backup RB Faces Tough Script 
 Healthy for tonight's matchup, McGowan continues operating as the primary backup behind Jonathan Taylor in Indianapolis. He brings momentum after scoring in back-to-back games, including his first NFL touchdown against Dallas earlier this month, while totaling 122 yards on 18 carries over his last two outings. Still, losing starting tackles Bernhard Raimann and Jalen Travis to injury threatens rushing efficiency.
 Despite climbing back to 45% roster ownership, McGowan holds just a 10% start rate, signaling a limited backup role. Our weekly projection lands at 5.0 PPR points on roughly seven carries for 30 yards and minimal receiving work. As heavy road underdogs in Houston, negative game script could restrict rushing touches, keeping him a bench stash or touchdown-dependent deep-league play.

 Outlook Jaylen Waddle 
 Jaylen Waddle vs. LV at home — probable to play in a modest scoring environment 
 Waddle is listed as probable after logging a full Wednesday practice ahead of Week 11, trending toward playing after suffering a concussion on November 8. Operating alongside Courtland Sutton as a starting perimeter receiver for Bo Nix, Waddle remains rostered in over 92% of leagues, with his start rate rebounding to 46% this week.
 Our weekly projection lands at 11.7 PPR points on roughly 4 catches, 46 receiving yards, and 6.5 targets against the 4–6 Raiders. With the 7–2 Broncos riding a five-game win streak as heavy home favorites in a projected low-scoring matchup, Denver could lean more on the run, making Waddle a flex option rather than a locked-in starter.
